Hi Product Hunt! I'm Kai, a musician. I made Clips while promoting my album. Song ads work best when you test several parts of the song, but cutting the same song fifteen ways in a video editor took a whole evening, so I'd make two and guess. Clips does that part. Drop in the song and your footage or photos, and it finds the tempo and every part, then makes a vertical lyric video for each one, cut on the beat with the words synced. Export them all at once, run them for a week, and keep the part that wins. It runs on your Mac, offline, so an unreleased song never leaves it. It's free to try (exports carry a small Clips tag), then $99 once. No subscription. I'd love to hear which part of your song you think would win, and what you'd want Clips to do next. Very cool concept! One thing I'm curious about: how well does the model handle off-key humming or rough vocal sketches? A lot of great ideas start messy. Congrats on the launch and looking forward to trying it out!

Nykee Zero

KuvMusic

@reddit\_shazan Thanks so much!

That’s exactly the use case I’m building around. HumToBeats does not expect a polished vocal take. The hum can be rough, off-key, or just a loose sketch of the melodic direction. The goal is to capture the intent: contour, rhythm, energy, and vibe, then use that as a creative signal for the generated beat. [...] That said, cleaner input usually gives the system a better starting point. A simple wordless hum with a clear rhythm or melody shape works best right now. If the input is extremely noisy or unclear, the result may need a few remix/regenerate passes.

I agree with you: a lot of good ideas start messy, so making the product tolerant of imperfect input is a big part of the roadmap.
